nodes.name: Software Development Lifecycle
nodes.note: Software development is an iterative process of understanding a problem, designing a solution, implementing it, evaluating evidence and maintaining the result.
nodes.hook: Take one application and identify evidence produced at every lifecycle stage.

nodes.name: Problem Analysis & Requirements
nodes.note: Analysis converts a real need into sufficiently precise requirements that can guide design and evaluation.
nodes.hook: Separate what the client asked for from the underlying problem they need solved.

nodes.name: Stakeholders
nodes.note: Stakeholders are people or groups who use, fund, operate, support or are affected by a system.
nodes.hook: Find one stakeholder whose needs conflict with the primary user.

nodes.name: Functional Requirements
nodes.note: Functional requirements specify behaviours or capabilities the system must provide.
nodes.hook: Rewrite a vague feature request as an observable system behaviour.

nodes.name: Non-functional Requirements
nodes.note: Non-functional requirements constrain qualities such as performance, security, reliability, accessibility and usability.
nodes.hook: Explain why fast is not a testable requirement until a threshold is defined.

nodes.name: Acceptance Criteria
nodes.note: Acceptance criteria state the evidence or conditions used to decide whether a requirement has been met.
nodes.hook: Write a pass/fail acceptance criterion for one requirement without describing implementation.

nodes.name: Software Design
nodes.note: Design turns requirements into a structured plan for components, data, algorithms, interfaces and interactions.
nodes.hook: Identify one design decision that should be made before writing code.

nodes.name: Decomposition
nodes.note: Decomposition breaks a complex problem into smaller responsibilities that can be reasoned about, implemented and tested.
nodes.hook: Break one feature into components until each part has one clear responsibility.

nodes.name: Algorithms
nodes.note: An algorithm is a defined sequence or structure of steps that transforms inputs into intended outputs.
nodes.hook: Express the same algorithm in plain English, pseudocode and code, then compare what changes.

nodes.name: Data Model
nodes.note: A data model defines the information a system stores and the relationships and constraints that give it meaning.
nodes.hook: Find duplicated data in a design and decide whether it should be represented once and referenced.

nodes.name: Interface Design
nodes.note: Interfaces define how users or software components exchange commands, inputs, outputs and state.
nodes.hook: Compare a user interface with an API: both expose capabilities but to different consumers.

nodes.name: Implementation
nodes.note: Implementation translates designs into executable software while preserving readability, correctness and maintainability.
nodes.hook: Show where an implementation choice satisfies a requirement rather than simply demonstrating syntax.

nodes.name: Variables & State
nodes.note: Variables associate names with values while program state describes information that changes during execution.
nodes.hook: Identify state that should be local to one operation rather than globally shared.

nodes.name: Control Flow
nodes.note: Sequence, selection and iteration determine which operations execute and in what order.
nodes.hook: Trace a user input through every branch that could affect the output.

nodes.name: Functions & Abstraction
nodes.note: Functions package behaviour behind a defined interface so logic can be reused, tested and understood independently.
nodes.hook: Refactor repeated code only when you can name the shared responsibility clearly.

nodes.name: Objects & Encapsulation
nodes.note: Object-oriented designs combine state and behaviour into objects and control how internal details are exposed.
nodes.hook: Explain what information an object should protect from unrelated parts of a program.

nodes.name: Error & Exception Handling
nodes.note: Error handling anticipates failure conditions and responds without leaving the system in an invalid or confusing state.
nodes.hook: Distinguish invalid user input from an unexpected programming defect.

nodes.name: Software Testing
nodes.note: Testing gathers evidence about whether software behaves as required under expected, boundary and failure conditions.
nodes.hook: Design a test from a requirement before looking at the implementation.

nodes.name: Unit Testing
nodes.note: Unit tests check small pieces of behaviour in isolation where practical.
nodes.hook: Choose a function whose output can be tested without launching the whole application.

nodes.name: Integration Testing
nodes.note: Integration testing checks whether components exchange data and control correctly when connected.
nodes.hook: Find a defect that neither component would reveal when tested completely alone.

nodes.name: System & Acceptance Testing
nodes.note: System and acceptance tests evaluate complete workflows against requirements and stakeholder expectations.
nodes.hook: Turn three acceptance criteria into end-to-end test cases.

nodes.name: Regression Testing
nodes.note: Regression testing checks that changes have not broken behaviour that previously worked.
nodes.hook: Explain why a bug fix needs tests outside the exact line that changed.

nodes.name: Defect Lifecycle
nodes.note: A useful defect process records reproduction, expected and actual behaviour, severity, fix and verification evidence.
nodes.hook: Write a defect report another developer can reproduce without speaking to you.

nodes.name: Version Control & Collaboration
nodes.note: Version control records changes and supports parallel collaboration, review and recovery through a graph of commits and references.
nodes.hook: Use repository history as evidence of development rather than treating Git as cloud storage.

nodes.name: Repository
nodes.note: A repository stores project history, references and tracked content.
nodes.hook: Explain what information Git retains that a folder copied to OneDrive does not.

nodes.name: Commit
nodes.note: A commit records a project snapshot with metadata and parent relationship, forming a history graph.
nodes.hook: Write a commit message that states the meaningful change rather than the file edited.

nodes.name: Branch
nodes.note: A branch is a movable reference to a commit used to develop work without immediately changing another line of development.
nodes.hook: Explain why a branch is cheap in Git compared with copying an entire project folder.

nodes.name: Merge
nodes.note: A merge combines histories and may create a merge commit when independent lines of development are joined.
nodes.hook: Use a graph to show why merge conflicts occur when histories touch the same context differently.

nodes.name: Rebase
nodes.note: Rebase replays commits onto a different base, producing a rewritten sequence of commit identities.
nodes.hook: Compare the history graph produced by merge with the graph produced by rebase.

nodes.name: Pull Request & Code Review
nodes.note: A pull request provides a collaboration surface for reviewing proposed changes before integration.
nodes.hook: Review the change against requirements and tests rather than commenting only on formatting.

nodes.name: Deployment & Maintenance
nodes.note: Software remains a living system after initial release and requires deployment, observation, correction and controlled change.
nodes.hook: List what can go wrong after software passes local testing.

nodes.name: Deployment
nodes.note: Deployment moves a tested software version into its intended environment with the required configuration and dependencies.
nodes.hook: Identify environment assumptions that can make works on my machine fail elsewhere.

nodes.name: Monitoring & Logging
nodes.note: Monitoring and logs provide operational evidence about behaviour, failures, performance and usage after deployment.
nodes.hook: Choose one event worth logging without collecting unnecessary personal data.

nodes.name: Maintenance
nodes.note: Maintenance includes correcting defects, adapting to changed environments and improving software while managing regression risk.
nodes.hook: Classify a change as corrective, adaptive or perfective and justify your classification.
